title.zh: 双面的门神，开端的守望者
title.en: The two-faced guardian of doorways and beginnings

summary.zh: 奥维德笔下手执钥匙与杖的双面神，自述曾是混沌；天地分开后获得神形，守护出入与开端。
summary.en: Ovid's two-faced god carries a key and staff, recalls a former existence as chaos, and watches over entrances and beginnings after the elements separate.

description.zh:
《岁时记》卷一中，诗人问雅努斯为什么有两张脸。神带着钥匙和杖现身，自述古时曾被称作混沌：火、气、水、土还挤在同一个未成形的团块里。元素分散，各自找到位置，他也由无定形的物质获得面容与肢体。两面相同的脸，是诗中留给这段往事的痕迹。

接下来的回答转向门与通道。门户本来就朝向内外两边；雅努斯也同时观看出入，掌管开与闭。他解释新年为什么适合说吉祥话、为什么人们先向他献上香与酒。这里呈现的是奥维德安排的诗人与神的问答，并非所有罗马资料都一致记载的神之传记。

双面形象还有独立的实物见证。大英博物馆藏钱币 1867,0212.84，约铸于公元前215至212年的罗马，一面是戴桂冠的蓄须雅努斯头像，另一面是船首。这枚钱币可以支持该图像的使用年代，却不能单凭图案证明奥维德的混沌故事当时已经流传。
description.en:
In Book 1 of the Fasti, Ovid asks why Janus has two faces. The god appears with a key and staff and recalls being called Chaos, when fire, air, water and earth were still mixed together. As the elements separate, he acquires a divine body. His matching faces retain a trace of that earlier condition.

Janus then explains his role through the two sides of a doorway. He watches entrances and departures and speaks about beginnings, New Year greetings and receiving incense and wine before other gods. This is an encounter staged within Ovid's poem, not a biography attested uniformly throughout Roman religion.

A separate material witness is British Museum coin 1867,0212.84, made at Rome around 215–212 BCE. It shows the laureate, bearded head of Janus on one side and a ship's prow on the other. The object documents the image; it cannot by itself establish that Ovid's account of primordial chaos was already being told at that date.

sources.zh: 奥维德《岁时记》卷一89—188行；J. G. Frazer 英译
sources.en: Ovid, Fasti 1.89–188; translated by J. G. Frazer

sources.zh: 大英博物馆：雅努斯与船首钱币，1867,0212.84
sources.en: British Museum: Janus and prow coin, 1867,0212.84
